label: rem:motivic-substrate-canonicity
title: Canonicity, realizations, and scope of the motivic substrate
html:
Remark. Canonicity, realizations, and scope of the motivic substrate

Canonicity of the substrate. Three observations factor through \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{mot}} rather than any single realization:

  • Mass formulas. The topological mass of a knot (motivic mass measure) is a class \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{mot}}(\beta) \in \widehat{\mathcal{M}}, not a real number. The real-valued mass arises only after applying \rho_\infty.
  • Adelic factorisation. The global zeta integral \mathcal{Z}(s) of the adelic substrate factorises as a restricted product \prod_v \zeta_v(s). This is the realization-tower factorisation \rho_{\mathrm{tot}} = \prod_v \rho_v applied to a single motivic class.
  • Habiro evaluation. The Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} is the universal target of the non-archimedean realizations of \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{mot}}. The functor \rho_p evaluates a motivic class at the level-p root of unity. The inverse limit over p recovers the Habiro completion.

Every algebraic invariant taking values in \mathbb{R}, \mathbb{Q}_p, or the Habiro ring is the realization at some place v of a single motivic class living in \widehat{\mathcal{M}}.

Relation to existing blocks.

  • The Frobenius–Hopf substrate is the algebraic-place realization. It forms a finite-type structure on \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{mot}}.
  • The adelic substrate is the place-decomposition \mathbb{A} = \mathbb{R} \times \prod_p' \mathbb{Q}_p indexing the realization tower. The adelic decomposition of a motivic class is the restricted product \rho_{\mathrm{tot}}([X]) = (\rho_v([X]))_v.
  • The arc space \mathcal{L}(X) provides the measurable space for motivic integration into \widehat{\mathcal{M}}. We derive the Kontsevich–Denef–Loeser motivic measure [kontsevich1995, denef-loeser2001] from this space.

Out of scope. Mixed motives, Bloch–Kato exact sequences, and full motivic Galois groups are not axiomatized here. The realization tower is presented purely as the family \{\rho_v\} of place-indexed evaluations; the categorical relationships among the \rho_v remain implicit.
